audit.why: Azir E (22/20.5/19/17.5/16s) shields him on the dash — committing burst into it wastes the Overwhelm window. R Emperor's Divide is a soldier wall/knockback, not a projectile, so W Rebuttal does not answer it.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Rebuttal spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — the shield-dash runs 22s at rank 1, 16s maxed. He burns it, you get the real window. - Conquering Sands is 14s early: poke between casts. - Emperor's Divide is 120s; without it his level 6 has no wall.

edits.before: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Shifting Sands shields him as it dashes — burst into it and it eats your combo. Force the E, then snare-volley the 22s window.

edits.before: Q-volley the last-hit, bank the overwhelm stacks, and keep W glowing — the chip is free while his best spells are hostages.
edits.after: Volley his step-up to last-hit — his Q is 14s and E 22s early, so the chip banks Overwhelm while he has no answer at 950 range.

edits.before: Burning Rebuttal on chip and then eating the full rotation it existed to return — the reflect is the matchup; spend it like a verdict.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is a charging soldier wall, not a projectile — Rebuttal will not stop the knockback, so keep your spacing even with W glowing.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by out-ranging you with stacked soldiers, eating burst with his E shield, and walling all-ins with R.
